001: Professor, do you have a moment to answer a question?
Sure, go ahead. What do you want to ask about?
It's about the exam content, I didn't quite understand the second part.
Oh, that part about the research methods, right?
That's right. I got confused about the difference between the two types.
No problem, let's go over it calmly now.
002: Could you take a look at my draft?
Of course, you can hand it to me. I'll read it carefully.
I wasn't sure if the introduction is too long.
Actually, it's pretty well balanced, but the conclusion needs more detail.
I see. Then I'll revise that part at home.
Good idea. If you need to, you can send it to me by email later.
003: Good morning, professor. I missed last class, can I get the material?
Good morning. No problem, but you need to justify your absence.
I was sick, I have the doctor's note here with me.
Perfect, then turn it in at the office and keep the material.
Thank you so much. I'll try hard not to fall behind.
I'm glad to see that commitment.
004: Professor, I couldn't understand the article you recommended.
Which part exactly left you confused?
The section about the research results was too technical for me.
I see. Try to focus on the graphs, they summarize the information well.
Oh, that helps a lot. I'll try reading it again with that tip.
If you still have questions, come find me next class.
005: Could you explain how the seminar will be evaluated?
Sure. You'll be evaluated on clarity and the content presented.
And can the group use slides during the presentation?
Yes, you can, but remember that the slides are just a support.
Perfect. Then we'll practice a lot before the day.
Great, I'm looking forward to seeing your presentation.
006: Professor, I wanted to talk about my grade on the last assignment.
Sure, have a seat. What would you like to know?
I thought my answer was complete, but I got a low grade.
Let me see here... You answered correctly, but you didn't go deep enough into the analysis.
I see. So I need to develop my arguments better.
Exactly. If you want, I can give you some extra references.
007: Do you have any reading recommendations for the thesis?
It depends on the topic. What area do you plan to explore?
I want to write about the impact of technology on education.
Great topic. Start with the classic authors and then look for recent articles.
I'll write that down. Could you recommend a specific author?
Sure, Paulo Freire is a great starting point for you.
008: Professor, I need to turn in an assignment early, is that possible?
Early? Usually students ask to delay, that's a new one.
It's because I'll be traveling during the week it's due, so I want to get it done before.
No problem, you can turn it in two days in advance.
Thank you so much, that takes a huge weight off my shoulders.
Don't mention it. Have a good trip and good work!
009: Can you help me with the formatting of the paper?
Sure, I can. Have you seen the ABNT rules in the course guide?
I saw them, but I was unsure about how to cite an interview.
Oh, that's a special case. Let me show you the correct example.
Perfect, that will help me a lot.
Any other questions, just come by.
010: Professor, I wanted to know if you're going to offer tutoring this semester.
Yes, I am, but only starting next month, on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
That's great! I need help with the statistics part.
Then come on Tuesday, I'll be reviewing the basic content.
Deal, I'll bring my questions in writing.
Perfect, that way we can make better use of the time.
